world.summary: Compact slice sea: 111 x 111 tiles generated from a mirrored ASCII quarter (assets/source/maps/sketch.ts -> slice-sea.tmj, 24 px Tiled tiles, new `hub` point object) via the unchanged map:build pipeline. Four islands, reefs, and midline shoal walls that open only inside the hub's disc. Report: neighbours 26.4 s, longest crossing 39.3 s, first dock <= 7.3 s, largest obstacle distance 9.9 tiles, 90.7% open sea. New validators (density: every navigable tile within SIGHT_RADIUS_TILES of land/shoal/dock, squared integers, edge not counted; hub: open sea near the centre, closing the disc of radius SIGHT/2 must raise or cut the shortest cost for every cross-island dock pair), each shown failing on a synthetic map in maps.test.ts; map:build prints the largest obstacle distance, open-sea share and each route's closest approach to the hub. Tuning: maxSpeed 39, acceleration 3, braking 3, drag 1, maxReverseSpeed 10, reverseAcceleration 1, dockMaxSpeed 15, dockRadius 384, turnRate 1; simulation tests measure time to full speed, braking distance, full turn and turning circle in px against the old tuning at 16 px (all within 25%), plus a docking sweep (headings 46/47, x every 16 sub-units across 3 tiles east of the dock, 2-4 tiles out, two start speeds) that always moors. Web: TILE_PIXELS 24 (content constant shared by Tiled and the client), art scaled, minimap 1.25 px/tile; sea keyboard latches a tap of E until the next read (unit test shows it docks). Protocol test-placement schema is now built from the map's size (createTestPlacementSchema). All test positions come from the map (hub row) and are checked for a clear hull line. sail-and-dock now docks into the shore corner at heading 46/47 with ahead+E held; sailTo sails in hops (turn at rest, hold ahead for a computed number of steps, coast) so it is robust to HUD lag. Checks run here: npm ci; npm run typecheck (pass); npm run test:unit (548 pass); npm run test:integration (37 pass); npm run build incl. smoke (pass); full Playwright suite with JSON reporter, 6 passed, check-report OK; tests/e2e/sea.spec.ts --repeat-each=5: 10/10 passed (sail-and-dock 5 in a row) at load average 6-8.
open_assumptions: No rock tile type was added (item 4 optional); obstacles are shoals and land only.
Tiled's tile size changed from 16 to 24 px so one TILE_PIXELS constant (content) is both the Tiled grid and the drawing scale.
protocol's exported testPlacementSchema was replaced by createTestPlacementSchema(bounds); the server builds it from its map. PROTOCOL_VERSION unchanged (test-only route).
The out-of-sight ships sit on the row 3 south of the hub: host at hub.x+1 (beside the gap in the south wall), guest at hub.x+14 (13 tiles apart), guest turns into the open water south of the row.
sailTo no longer steers continuously; it hops from rest (turn, timed ahead hold from shipTuning, coast to a stop) and never brakes.

Observed, not fixed (out of scope): if the page stalls >250 ms the server lapses input to neutral, resetting mooredThrottle; a moored ship then casts off if ahead stays held after E is released. The browser test releases ahead before E.

# Decisions: sea-compact

From the operator session of 2026-09-24. The operator answered the planning questions, and the assistant chose the details under their instruction to "make the ideal choice".

## Decisions

- The operator's playtest verdict: the online duel "works and it's good, can be smoother", so the combat spike passes and duel smoothness is tuned later. On the sea: "have a denser map and reduce the scale". This feature does that before `encounters-theft`, because encounters need ships that meet, and encounter tests depend on map distances.
- §3's travel times stay binding (neighbours 20–40 s, longest crossing ≤ 90 s). Shrinking the world is only legal if ships slow down, so full speed drops from 5 to 3 tiles a second, and the map shrinks to at most 112 × 112 tiles (under a quarter of today's area).
- Corrected after design challenge attempt 1. The tile's 256 sub-units, the 64 headings and `turnRate` 1 stay unchanged: 1 is already the minimum, and the claim tests depend on 256. So full speed is 39 sub-units per step (3.05 tiles/s), and handling is judged on screen: time to full speed, stopping distance, 3.2 s per full turn, and the turning circle in pixels.
- "Ships meet" becomes a check, not a hope: every neighbour route passes within sight of one central `hub` point, because shoals block the direct routes along the edges. At about 3 tiles/s, the detour through the centre also keeps neighbours inside §3's 20–40 s.
- Corrected after design challenge attempt 2. The sea keyboard dropped quick taps (it polls held keys), so it now records taps like the duel keyboard: a player-facing fix, not just test hygiene. `sail-and-dock` docks by holding ahead and E on the dock's axis, a rule already tested in the simulation, rather than timed taps. The hub disc radius is half the sight radius, so ships inside it see each other, and the check blocks the disc for every dock pair instead of rebuilding one path. The dock reach stays at 384 or more.
- Corrected after design challenge attempt 3. Driving in on the dock's axis only moors when the ship is exactly aligned: off-axis, it slides along the coast at full speed or grounds on the land beside the dock. The test now aims into a corner of the shore at a fixed heading tilted toward the land, which moors from any lateral offset, and a unit test sweeps the offsets. The out-of-sight row runs parallel to a wall with turning room, and hub sight is stated for tile centres.
- "Reduce the scale" also means drawing larger. Tiles go from 16 to about 24 px, so the 10-tile sight circle fits on the 800 × 560 view and on-screen speed stays about the same (80 → 72 px/s). The sight radius itself stays 10 tiles.
- Density is a validator, not a judgement: no navigable tile may be farther than the sight radius from a non-sea tile, and routes are funnelled through channels. This follows §3 ("Remove empty stretches before adding more sailing mechanics"), so there are no new mechanics (slow zones, currents).
- Still four small islands (§18 stage 2). A `rock` tile type for outcrops and landmarks is optional; shoals alone are acceptable.
- The flaky `sail-and-dock` browser test (seen in duel-online-fixes-001's worker phase) is fixed here, since this feature rewrites its route anyway. The final approach is in `world-task.md` item 8, the only authority on it. It must pass 5 repeats.
- One fullstack lane (`world`) with all five checks and all six browser scenario ids. The owned paths list the sea files one by one, so the assistant's parallel ledger and claim fixes (`packages/*/src/objectives`, `packages/*/src/claim`) stay disjoint.
- Every acceptance item names its test, because most earlier blocked reviews came from acceptance items without one.

## Assumptions

- The operator confirmed the objectives-ledger defaults: the repeat-win gold window counts from any previous win, paid or not; a winner who leaves during the 5 s theft choice takes nothing.
- The encounters slice will run the duel inside `MatchRoom` as a simulation object, as §14 requires ("Duels are isolated simulation objects within that room"), reusing the `simulation/netcode` core. The standalone `DuelRoom` stays as the practice arena. This is recorded for `encounters-theft` and doesn't change this feature.
- The protocol version stays: the message shapes don't change, and the web and server always ship together.
- The handling numbers (acceleration, braking, drag, turn rate, dock radius and speed) are the worker's to rescale within about ±25 % of today's feel.

## Deferred

- `encounters-theft` (slice 4), with its own grill: the duel embedded in `MatchRoom`, challenge and grapple, reservation, theft through the ledger, and §12's disconnects.
- The 12-island alpha map, slow-zone hazards and art.
- Duel smoothness tuning (input delay, interpolation) after more playtests.

concerns.message: The corner approach in item 8 does not moor from 'any lateral offset'. It only works when the hull starts east of the land beside the dock with room for its drift. Heading 47 at full speed moves dx=-3 and dy=-38 per step (heading 46: dx=-7), so over the 3-tile run the ship drifts about 64 sub-units west (about 150 at heading 46). If the hull's left edge ends up in column dock.tileX-1, it hits the land beside the dock from the south. It then slides west along the island's south shore at full speed, is never grounded on both axes, and never moors. It also only works if the tiles north of the approach columns are land (row dock.tileY-1 for columns dock.tileX+1 to +2). If the shore steps back there, the ship passes the dock row and grounds one row higher. From there `dockInReach`'s hull-path check cuts the land corner, so it refuses to moor. The test's map check only covers the dock's own row.
concerns.consequence: The browser test can time out whenever sailTo stops at the dock.tileX+1 waypoint on its west side: `within: TILE` allows up to 256 sub-units of error, and the ship keeps coasting while it turns. The unit sweep 'across the tile' would still pass, because it never starts from the band that fails. That repeats the flake this item is meant to fix, in the fourth revision.

concerns.message: Item 8's sweep should start from the band sailTo actually leaves the ship in, not only one tile's width. That means start x from dock.tileX*256 to (dock.tileX+3)*256, a starting speed of 0 and sailTo's arrival speed, and the turn from the previous leg's heading. The browser test should use +2, or coast to a stop before turning (a ship can turn at speed 0), and assert the minimum safe x taken from the sweep.
concerns.consequence: Without this, the unit test proves the rule where the ship never actually starts, and the 5-repeat run becomes the only real check.

concerns.message: 'Within ±25 % of today's' handling (time to full speed, stopping distance, turning circle in pixels) needs today's values (64/4/8/2/24, 16 px) kept as a named baseline in the test. Once `shipTuning` changes, the old numbers no longer exist anywhere in the code.
concerns.consequence: A test that derives both sides from the current `shipTuning` becomes a tautology and can't catch retuning that moves outside the ±25 % band.

concerns.message: One hand-built layout has to meet many coupled constraints: the hub cut for every dock pair, density with no credit for the map edge, a neighbour floor of at least 61 path tiles (so every dock sits at least ~31 octile tiles from the hub gap), spawn slots outside the islands' bounding box, a south dock with land to the west, sea to the east and a shoal bar to sail around, and the clear out-of-sight row beside a wall.
concerns.consequence: Fitting these one at a time against `map:build`'s validators can take many iterations. That risks the two-hour stop condition, or a map that passes the validators but has no usable test geometry, which means reworking the tests.

challenge.simpler_alternative: Write the sketch script to draw one 56 × 56 quadrant (one island with its docks, two spawn slots, obstacles, and half of each midline wall ending at the hub gap) and rotate it three times by 90° around the centre. Neighbour times, spawn-to-dock times and density then match for all four quadrants by construction, so only one quadrant needs tuning against the validators. Have the script also assert the two test geometries (the corner-dock tiles, including row dock.tileY-1 east of the dock, and the out-of-sight row with its turning side), so a layout change breaks the sketch rather than the browser tests.
challenge.cheap_experiment: Before drawing the map, write the corner-approach sweep as a simulation unit test on a tiny synthetic map: a dock with land to the north and west, and sea to the east and south. Using the proposed tuning (maxSpeed 39, accel 3, drag 1, dockMaxSpeed about 15), start the ship 3 tiles south with start x from dock.tileX*256 to (dock.tileX+3)*256 in 16-sub-unit steps. Try headings 46 and 47, and starting states of speed 0, and speed about 20 turning in from heading 32. Record the smallest start x that still moors. This takes minutes. It settles +1 against +2, whether to coast to a stop before turning, and what safe band the browser test should assert.

# Task: world

## Goal

Make the slice sea compact and dense, so ships meet. Today the map is 224 × 208 tiles and 99.2 % open sea: four small islands sit in its corners, and with a 10-tile sight radius players rarely see each other. The operator's playtest verdict: "a denser map, and reduce the scale". Shrink the world, slow the ships so §3's travel times still hold, fill the sea with obstacles and landmarks that funnel routes together, and draw everything larger so the sight circle fits the screen.

## Context

- Read `docs/spec.md` §3 (sea, islands, travel-time targets, "Remove empty stretches before adding more sailing mechanics"), §2 ("Spawn fairness") and §18 stage 2 (four small islands). Then read `docs/architecture.md` (map pipeline, sailing, docking, visibility), `assets/source/maps/README.md`, `packages/content/src/sailing.ts`, `seaMap.ts`, `seaValidation.ts`, `maps.test.ts`, `scripts/build-map.ts`, `packages/simulation/src/step.ts`, `apps/web/src/camera.ts`, `seaScene.ts`, `fog.ts` and `tests/e2e/sea.spec.ts`.
- The verifier runs `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration`, `npm run build` (ending with `scripts/smoke-build.ts`) and `npx --no-install playwright test --config=tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts`. Playwright's Chromium for `@playwright/test` 1.63.0 is installed and shared read-only; never run `playwright install`.
- Another change runs at the same time in `packages/simulation/src/objectives`, `packages/simulation/src/claim`, `packages/content/src/objectives`, `packages/content/src/claim`, `docs/claim.md` and `docs/objectives.md`. Never touch those paths.
- **This machine is shared by several runs. Never stop processes by name pattern (`pkill -f`, `killall`, and so on). Stop only the PIDs you started.**

## Constraints

- Owned paths as in `policy.json`. Keep the existing pipeline (Tiled `.tmj` → `npm run map:build` → `packages/content/src/maps/sliceSea.ts`, with its drift test), structure, names and patterns. Don't hand-edit the generated module.
- Keep the simulation integer and deterministic, the server the only writer, zod-validated protocol messages, the admission layers, the visibility boundary and docking's rules (interact with any throttle held, the dock hint, cast off on reversing throttle).
- The duel is untouched. Keep every browser scenario id and every existing test. Tests you must change because coordinates or speeds changed keep their intent, and they take positions from the map or content constants rather than new hard-coded numbers.
- Tests drive input like players do: they hold and tap keys, and wait on what a player sees (the HUD, the dock hint). They never set the speed or reach into state.
- Placeholder art only: coloured tiles and shapes drawn by Phaser, no image files.
- You may generate the `.tmj` from a small sketch script under `assets/source/maps/` (for example a symmetric ASCII layout) rather than hand-placing tiles in Tiled. The `.tmj` stays the committed source that `npm run map:build` reads, and the README says how to regenerate it.
- Out of scope: new sailing mechanics (slow zones, currents, wind), ruins, loot, encounters, more islands.

## Acceptance

Each item names the test that proves it.

1. **Smaller world and slower ships.** The map is at most 112 × 112 tiles. `maxSpeed` is 39 sub-units per world step (3.05 tiles a second; 3 exactly isn't an integer). Keep `SUB_UNITS_PER_TILE` (256), `HEADING_COUNT` (64), the heading table and `turnRate` (1, already the minimum) unchanged; the claim code's tests depend on 256. Rescale only acceleration, reverse speed and acceleration, braking, drag and the dock speed. Keep the dock reach (`dockRadius`) at 384 sub-units or more: it doesn't depend on speed. Handling is measured on screen, which the larger scale (item 6) preserves: time to full speed and stopping distance in tiles stay within about ±25 % of today's, a full turn still takes 3.2 s, and the turning circle in pixels at the new scale stays within about ±25 % of today's in pixels at 16 px. Simulation unit tests assert each of these against the named constants, not literals.

# Decisions: sea-compact

From the operator session of 2026-09-24. The operator answered the planning questions, and the assistant chose the details under their instruction to "make the ideal choice".

## Decisions

- The operator's playtest verdict: the online duel "works and it's good, can be smoother", so the combat spike passes and duel smoothness is tuned later. On the sea: "have a denser map and reduce the scale". This feature does that before `encounters-theft`, because encounters need ships that meet, and encounter tests depend on map distances.
- §3's travel times stay binding (neighbours 20–40 s, longest crossing ≤ 90 s). Shrinking the world is only legal if ships slow down, so full speed drops from 5 to 3 tiles a second, and the map shrinks to at most 112 × 112 tiles (under a quarter of today's area).
- Corrected after design challenge attempt 1. The tile's 256 sub-units, the 64 headings and `turnRate` 1 stay unchanged: 1 is already the minimum, and the claim tests depend on 256. So full speed is 39 sub-units per step (3.05 tiles/s), and handling is judged on screen: time to full speed, stopping distance, 3.2 s per full turn, and the turning circle in pixels.
- "Ships meet" becomes a check, not a hope: every neighbour route passes within sight of one central `hub` point, because shoals block the direct routes along the edges. At about 3 tiles/s, the detour through the centre also keeps neighbours inside §3's 20–40 s.
- Corrected after design challenge attempt 2. The sea keyboard dropped quick taps (it polls held keys), so it now records taps like the duel keyboard: a player-facing fix, not just test hygiene. `sail-and-dock` docks by holding ahead and E on the dock's axis, a rule already tested in the simulation, rather than timed taps. The hub disc radius is half the sight radius, so ships inside it see each other, and the check blocks the disc for every dock pair instead of rebuilding one path. The dock reach stays at 384 or more.
- Corrected after design challenge attempt 3. Driving in on the dock's axis only moors when the ship is exactly aligned: off-axis, it slides along the coast at full speed or grounds on the land beside the dock. The test now aims into a corner of the shore at a fixed heading tilted toward the land, which moors from any lateral offset, and a unit test sweeps the offsets. The out-of-sight row runs parallel to a wall with turning room, and hub sight is stated for tile centres.
- "Reduce the scale" also means drawing larger. Tiles go from 16 to about 24 px, so the 10-tile sight circle fits on the 800 × 560 view and on-screen speed stays about the same (80 → 72 px/s). The sight radius itself stays 10 tiles.
- Density is a validator, not a judgement: no navigable tile may be farther than the sight radius from a non-sea tile, and routes are funnelled through channels. This follows §3 ("Remove empty stretches before adding more sailing mechanics"), so there are no new mechanics (slow zones, currents).
- Still four small islands (§18 stage 2). A `rock` tile type for outcrops and landmarks is optional; shoals alone are acceptable.
- The flaky `sail-and-dock` browser test (seen in duel-online-fixes-001's worker phase) is fixed here, since this feature rewrites its route anyway. The final approach is in `world-task.md` item 8, the only authority on it. It must pass 5 repeats.
- One fullstack lane (`world`) with all five checks and all six browser scenario ids. The owned paths list the sea files one by one, so the assistant's parallel ledger and claim fixes (`packages/*/src/objectives`, `packages/*/src/claim`) stay disjoint.
- Every acceptance item names its test, because most earlier blocked reviews came from acceptance items without one.

- The encounters slice will run the duel inside `MatchRoom` as a simulation object, as §14 requires ("Duels are isolated simulation objects within that room"), reusing the `simulation/netcode` core. - The protocol version stays: the message shapes don't change, and the web and server always ship together.

scenarios.description: One browser creates a private match from the landing page; the HUD shows the code, the protocol version, one player and a connected status.
Two browsers join the same private match with their ships in sight of each other; one sails with the keyboard and the other browser's view shows that ship at the new server-authoritative position.
A browser sails its ship around a shoal to an island dock with the keyboard and docks there; the HUD shows the dock and the ship stops at it.
Two browsers in one match with their ships out of sight of each other: neither view lists or draws the other ship until one sails within the sight radius, and it disappears again when it sails away.

One browser opens a practice duel against the dummy, lands a jab and then a keyboard throw (J then K a frame apart); the dummy's health bar and the HUD drop by the move data's damage, and hitboxes can be shown.

Two browsers: one creates a duel, the other joins by its code; after the countdown the first lands a strike on the second, and both views show the same authoritative health, round clock and result, with the connection line showing input delay and corrections.

completion.summary: Compact slice sea: 111 x 111 tiles generated from a mirrored ASCII quarter (assets/source/maps/sketch.ts -> slice-sea.tmj, 24 px Tiled tiles, new `hub` point object) via the unchanged map:build pipeline. Four islands, reefs, and midline shoal walls that open only inside the hub's disc. Report: neighbours 26.4 s, longest crossing 39.3 s, first dock <= 7.3 s, largest obstacle distance 9.9 tiles, 90.7% open sea. New validators (density: every navigable tile within SIGHT_RADIUS_TILES of land/shoal/dock, squared integers, edge not counted; hub: open sea near the centre, closing the disc of radius SIGHT/2 must raise or cut the shortest cost for every cross-island dock pair), each shown failing on a synthetic map in maps.test.ts; map:build prints the largest obstacle distance, open-sea share and each route's closest approach to the hub. Tuning: maxSpeed 39, acceleration 3, braking 3, drag 1, maxReverseSpeed 10, reverseAcceleration 1, dockMaxSpeed 15, dockRadius 384, turnRate 1; simulation tests measure time to full speed, braking distance, full turn and turning circle in px against the old tuning at 16 px (all within 25%), plus a docking sweep (headings 46/47, x every 16 sub-units across 3 tiles east of the dock, 2-4 tiles out, two start speeds) that always moors. Web: TILE_PIXELS 24 (content constant shared by Tiled and the client), art scaled, minimap 1.25 px/tile; sea keyboard latches a tap of E until the next read (unit test shows it docks). Protocol test-placement schema is now built from the map's size (createTestPlacementSchema). All test positions come from the map (hub row) and are checked for a clear hull line. sail-and-dock now docks into the shore corner at heading 46/47 with ahead+E held; sailTo sails in hops (turn at rest, hold ahead for a computed number of steps, coast) so it is robust to HUD lag. Checks run here: npm ci; npm run typecheck (pass); npm run test:unit (548 pass); npm run test:integration (37 pass); npm run build incl. smoke (pass); full Playwright suite with JSON reporter, 6 passed, check-report OK; tests/e2e/sea.spec.ts --repeat-each=5: 10/10 passed (sail-and-dock 5 in a row) at load average 6-8.

protocol's exported testPlacementSchema was replaced by createTestPlacementSchema(bounds); the server builds it from its map. PROTOCOL_VERSION unchanged (test-only route).

sailTo no longer steers continuously; it hops from rest (turn, timed ahead hold from shipTuning, coast to a stop) and never brakes.
